2608.03699.title: TARL: Transaction-Aware Reliable Ledgers for Executable Memory Management in Long-Term Agents
2608.03699.paper_summary: Persistent memory helps long-term agents retain knowledge, yet a single update error can repeatedly distort future retrieval and reasoning. Most existing systems reduce memory updating to a binary Write/Hold decision, which cannot distinguish whether new information should be added, ignored, used to revise an outdated belief, rejected as unreliable, or deferred for verification. These choices may share the same binary label while producing fundamentally different memory states. We introduce TARL, a memory state update framework that maps each statement to one of five executable actions. TARL identifies the affected memory, resolves its temporal scope, compares source reliability, and updates accepted, pending, and rejected ledgers. It is further trained by comparing the memory states produced by alternative update operations, encouraging the model to select the operation that leads to the correct result. We also introduce TARL-Mem, a benchmark with fine-grained action labels and next-state targets. Across in-domain, cross-source, temporal, counterfactual, and sequential evaluations, TARL improves action prediction and state recovery, reduces memory pollution, preserves conflicting evidence, and limits cumulative corruption. The complete model implementation is provided in the supplementary material.
2608.03699.paper_summary_zh: 持久記憶幫助長期代理保持知識，然而單一的更新錯誤可能會反覆扭曲未來的檢索和推理。大多數現有系統將記憶更新簡化為二元的寫入/保持決策，這無法區分新信息是應該被添加、忽略、用來修正過時的信念、被拒絕為不可靠，還是延遲驗證。這些選擇可能共享相同的二元標籤，同時產生根本不同的記憶狀態。我們介紹了 TARL，一個記憶狀態更新框架，將每個陳述映射到五個可執行動作之一。TARL 確定受影響的記憶，解決其時間範圍，比較來源的可靠性，並更新接受、待定和拒絕的賬本。它進一步通過比較不同更新操作產生的記憶狀態進行訓練，鼓勵模型選擇導致正確結果的操作。我們還介紹了 TARL-Mem，一個具有細粒度動作標籤和下一狀態目標的基準。在域內、跨來源、時間、反事實和序列評估中，TARL 改進了動作預測和狀態恢復，減少了記憶污染，保留了衝突證據，並限制了累積腐敗。完整的模型實現提供在補充材料中。
